source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record 1980;55(18):129-130 - Cholera in 1979 (with WER 1979;54(17) Cholera in 1978, Table 1)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1978-01-01..1978-12-31. Source states: 'There was a reappearance of cholera in Ivory Coast, which had been free since 1971, and Mozambique, unaffected since 1977, had a large outbreak during this year [1979]. (WER 1980;55(18), 'Cholera in 1979'); WER 1979;54(17) 'Cholera in 1978' Table 1 'Cases of Cholera Notified to WHO, 1978' lists 18 African countries, Mozambique not among them.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. Replaces retracted Index 4 (which cited only Aragon 1994). Three independent WHO lines of evidence: (1) the WHO 1979 review states Mozambique was 'unaffected since 1977' (FR 'indemne depuis 1977'); (2) the WHO 1978 notification table omits Mozambique; (3) all 51 WER 1978 weekly issues (IRIS vol. 53) were checked - the only Mozambique IHR notification in 1978 is PLAGUE (Tete, Mutarara Deleg. S., 12 cases, 28 Oct-3 Nov 1978, WER 53(46) p.8), so the IHR reporting channel was functioning. Consistent with Aragon 1994 Tabela 1 (1978 incidence 0,0; metadata 2) and with ./data/MOZ/cholera_data_jhu.csv (no 1978 row; 1977 = 18, 1979 = 4564). Surveillance: operational (MoH Boletim Epidemiologico Semanal + IHR notification). reporting_date = issue date of WER 1980 No 18 (approx.).
